summary: CLI silently executes shell commands returned by a remote LLM on push failure
details: gitquickpush.js catches failures from `gitquickpush push` and POSTs the error text plus `git status` output to a remote LLM (Google Generative AI at generativelanguage.googleapis.com, or router.huggingface.co) using either a user-supplied key or two hardcoded Google Generative AI API keys shipped as the default fallback (`AQ.Ab8RN6...`). The JSON response's `commandsToRun` array is then iterated with `execSync(cmd, { stdio: 'ignore' })`, so whatever shell commands the model returns run silently in the user's repository with no confirmation and suppressed output. The invoker requested a git push, not arbitrary command execution; anything that influences the model output — prompt injection via the git error text, a swapped `baseURL`, or use/compromise of the shipped keys — produces silent code execution on the installer's machine. The hardcoded Google API keys are also redistributed to every installer of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
